lesson.subject: general-knowledge
lesson.title: Ancient Egypt and the Nile
lesson.summary: Find out how the River Nile shaped ancient Egypt and what writing, kingdoms and tombs tell us.
lesson.unit: Topic 9: Ancient Egypt and the Nile
learning_objectives: Place ancient Egypt in time using BCE
Describe what the Rosetta Stone and tomb discoveries taught us

standards.text: Study the achievements of the earliest civilisations: ancient Egypt, its rivers, kingdoms and writing

success_criteria: I can say why the Nile was important
I can read a BCE timeline
I can say what the Rosetta Stone helped us do
lesson.real_life: Egypt and Pakistan as river civilisations, Cairo in Islamic history, and the Rosetta Stone in the British Museum in London.

warm_up.prompt: Fertile land is good for growing crops.

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: why did the Nile matter so much?
blocks.say: Today we travel back about 5,000 years to ancient Egypt, beside the great River Nile.

blocks.alt: Three pyramids on desert sand at sunset with golden rays across the sky and modern buildings in the foreground
blocks.caption: The pyramids of Giza at sunset, near Cairo in Egypt.
blocks.credit: Photo by Ruben Hanssen on Unsplash
blocks.say: The pyramids of Giza are about 4,500 years old. Egyptians built them near the Nile.

blocks.markdown: The Nile flows through several countries, not only Egypt.
blocks.say: The Nile is one of the longest rivers in the world. It flows north to the Mediterranean Sea.

blocks.markdown: A **civilisation** is a society with cities, trade and organised rules.
blocks.say: Rain falls far to the south. The water travels through desert to reach Egypt.

blocks.say: Every year the Nile flooded. It left dark, rich mud on the land beside it.

blocks.title: Hina on the Nile
blocks.transcript: Hina drifts down the Nile on a felucca, a small sailing boat. The Nile flows north towards the sea. Dark mud lies on the banks after the flood. Seeds grow well in this fertile mud. Farmers grow wheat, barley and flax beside the river. Beyond the green banks lies dry desert. In the distance she sees the pyramids of Giza. Hina understands. The Nile was a gift to Egypt.
blocks.caption: Hina drifts down the Nile on a felucca and sees why dark mud made the banks fertile.

points: Egyptians were farmers by the river

blocks.markdown: Upper Egypt is upstream, in the south. Lower Egypt is the delta, in the north.
blocks.say: Egypt began as two lands. Upper Egypt lay in the south. Lower Egypt lay in the north.

blocks.markdown: A **pharaoh** was a king or queen of ancient Egypt.
blocks.say: About 3100 BCE the two lands joined under one king. Later rulers were called pharaohs.
